sections.content: To say how much of a food or drink, Hungarian names a container or a measure and then the food, in this order: number + container + food. There is nothing like “of”: *egy pohár víz* is “a glass of water”.

sections.title: Numbers and the container
sections.content: The container stays singular after a number, as after every number you know: *két pohár*, *három üveg*. The food stays in its basic form, too: *két pohár víz*, not *poharak* or *vizek*. *Sok* (a lot) and *kevés* (little) work the same way: *sok tej*, *kevés kenyér*.

items.english: There is a glass of water.
There are two bottles of wine.
There is a kilo of apples.
There is a piece of cheese.
There are three cups of tea.

sections.content: In English the food comes after “of”. In Hungarian there is no “of”: the container is simply placed in front of the food: *csésze tea* (cup tea).
